title: Second Contact
description:
Day two on the same fictional training host. The `operator` account was left with more artefacts:

```
$ cd /home/operator
$ ls -la
total 24
drwxr-xr-x 3 operator operator 4096 Nov 12 08:40 .
drwxr-xr-x 3 root     root     4096 Nov 11 08:55 ..
-rw-r--r-- 1 operator operator  184 Nov 11 09:00 welcome.txt
-rw-r--r-- 1 operator operator  310 Nov 12 08:38 notes.txt
```

The training log claims the real session token is still on this host, but the instructor did not leave it where a plain `ls` shows it. The encoding changed as well.

This exercise only uses a fictional, isolated host. The goal is to practise hidden-file discovery and a second encoding on top of the first contact.
objective: Find the hidden session token in the operator home directory, decode it and submit the value as HC{value}.

hints.text: `ls` hides dotfiles by default. Add the `-a` flag to see every entry in the directory.
The live token is stored in a file called `.session_token` inside `/home/operator`.
That file holds a hex string. `xxd -r -p .session_token` turns it back into readable text.
